text:
Closest evidence comes from interaction-only models, rather than one verified SASRec extension covering every requested control. [PAN](https://arxiv.org/html/2006.15346v2) pools the same session through recent-intent and historical-preference attentions: overlapping evidence, not disjoint histories. It reports history-only, average-pooling, concatenation, product and learned-gate ablations; Diginetica Recall@20 is 46.97 for history-only, 49.99 for averaging and 50.69 for gating. No recent-only result appears in those tables. [TLSRec](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf) compares dimension-wise time gating against averaging and attention fusion. Its “-S”/“-L” variants remove attention components, not entire preference branches. Neither provides the complete requested ablation matrix.

For implementation, [original SASRec](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/modules.py) masks future positions and padding. Adapting historical pooling to all-position SASRec training requires prefix-specific queries and pools: restricting keys alone cannot repair a query computed from future interactions. Recommended control: recent positions max(1,t−w+1)…t versus older positions 1…t−w, alongside an overlapping-history variant. Preserve repeated interaction occurrences; deduplication changes frequency evidence. [RepeatNet’s implementation](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/RecBole/blob/master/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/repeatnet.py) provides a separate repeat/explore design, aggregating repeat probability onto item identities; this addresses a different problem from timescale fusion.

Gate-collapse remedies were not established by these ablations. Proposed diagnostics: gate saturation/variance, branch norms and gradients, representation similarity, and branch-removal sensitivity. Compare recent-only, history-only, fixed fusion and learned gating under matched training. For residual initialization, [ReZero](https://www.auai.org/uai2021/pdf/uai2021.519.pdf) supports h=h_SASRec+αF with α initially zero; branch gradients initially vanish. Avoid simultaneously zeroing α and F’s output projection, which can leave both without a learning signal. These are proposed adaptation controls, not demonstrated RecHarness gains.
